title: Iran: Five protest-related arbitrary executions in one week must spur global action
content:
In response to the Iranian authorities arbitrarily executing five people convicted in relation to the January 2026 protests in the space of a week, between 30 September and 5 October – Ali Hemmati Sistanian, Alireza Raisi, Alireza Sepahi, Majid Nikandish and Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi – following grossly unfair torture-tainted trials, Diana Eltahawy, Deputy Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa at Amnesty International said: 

“The arbitrary executions of these five young men serves as another chilling reminder of how the Iranian authorities weaponize the death penalty to render the cost of dissent so high that it terrorizes the population into silence and deters further mass uprisings challenging their repressive decades-long rule.

title: Still, We Rise: a new EU-funded programme to strengthen women’s influence in peace processes
content:
On 6 October 2026, the EU-funded programme Still, We Rise: Reclaiming and Transforming the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Agenda was launched in Brussels. The event brought together policymakers, peacebuilding practitioners, civil society representatives and experts to discuss how women’s influence and leadership in peace processes can be strengthened at a time when the need has never been greater.

The programme is being launched against a backdrop of rising violent conflict worldwide and continuing barriers to women’s meaningful participation in efforts to build peace. Despite decades of advocacy and evidence demonstrating the value of inclusive peace processes, women remain significantly underrepresented in formal negotiations and mediation efforts. In 2024, women made up just 7 per cent of negotiators and 14 per cent of mediators in formal peace processes, and many talks included no women at all.

Discussions at the launch highlighted a key message: women are already building peace. The task now is to ensure they have the influence, resources and political support to shape peace processes and outcomes. Photo: Johanna de Tessières

title: Suomi: Tuhlailu seis, haluamme yhä lisäleikkauksia EU-budjettiin
content:
Eurooppaministeri Joakim Strandin (r.) mukaan EU:n puheenjohtajamaan Irlannin esittämä noin 140 miljardin euron leikkaus tulevaan EU-budjettiin ei lähellekään riitä Suomelle.

Strandin mukaan leikkauksen tulee olla suurempi.

- Tarkkoja numeroita en tässä kohtaa neuvotteluita vielä kerro. Kuten aikaisemmin on puhuttu, useampi sata miljardia komission 1 900 miljardin esityksestä tulisi tulla alas. Eli vielä on matkaa, Strand sanoi tiedotustilaisuudessaan tiistaina.

Ministerin mukaan Suomi on tyytyväinen budjettiesityksen prioriteetteihin, mutta esityksen kokonaistaso on liian korkea. Toisaalta esimerkiksi kilpailukyvystä ollaan Strandin mukaan leikkaamassa liikaa.

- Se on meidän mielestämme väärä kohde. Meitä myös harmittaa, että olisi voitu leikata enemmän perinteisestä koheesiopolitiikasta.

IRLANNIN eurooppaministeri Thomas Byrne puolusteli aiemmin tiistaina maan viikonloppuna julkistamaa esitystä EU:n vuosien 2028-34 budjetiksi.

Byrne kommentoi budjettiesityksestä käytyä keskustelua saapuessaan EU-maiden eurooppaministerien kokoukseen Luxemburgissa.

title: After flood disasters, Nepal needs clear numbers on aid and a reconstruction plan
content:
Nepali communities live in the shadow of natural hazards, where uncertainty and fear are daily realities

Originally published on Global Voices

Settlements across the Tadi River, Devighat in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.

Forty-six days later, just when Nepal was trying to recover from the Bhotekoshi flash flood, which struck the Nepal–Tibet border regions, affecting Rasuwa and Nuwakot, another landslide-induced flood hit Chumnubri, Gorkha, on October 11, 2026. This latest disaster has added to the wounds of communities who live in the shadow of natural hazards, where uncertainty and fear are daily realities.

The climate-related disaster in Nuwakot has devastated a once-popular tourist landscape, destroying its natural beauty and economic opportunities, with settlements heartbreakingly reduced to rubble and vital infrastructure, including roads, bridges and hydro-power facilities, washed away. The full death toll remains officially unconfirmed.

Survivors still come to search for their belongings in Devighatm, Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.

title: A Nobel for Justice as Washington Moves Against the World Court
content:
Navi Pillay’s Peace Prize and sweeping US sanctions on the International Criminal Court place two opposing views of international law before the world.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | THE HAGUE 13 October 2026 (IDN) — On the same day that the United States announced sanctions against the International Criminal Court as an institution, the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded its Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, a former ICC judge and United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.

The coincidence could hardly have been more pointed. One decision honoured a jurist who has spent much of her life trying to hold perpetrators of grave crimes accountable. The other threatened the Court created to prosecute genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes when national courts fail or refuse to act.

The Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 prize to the 85-year-old South African “for her efforts to promote peace and international law”. It said international law was under intense pressure and the institutions established to uphold it were being attacked.

title: €170 Million a Year in France Alone: The Price of Leaving a Secondary Publication Right Out of the ERA Act
content:
Maximising the impact of research is at the heart of the European Union’s plans to boost competitiveness and find solutions to both economic and societal challenges. In this, finding the most cost-effective way of enabling the sharing of insights and research outputs plays a central role, both within institutions and with the private partners and members of the public with whom they work. We also know that open access to research is particularly important for SMEs, as drivers of competitiveness.

There are serious and widely-held concerns about the sustainability of the way in which scholarly communication works today, with higher and higher costs and fewer and fewer freedoms to use the outputs from publicly funded research.

Despite this, the EU may be on the point of taking a step that risks fundamentally undermining these efforts, putting the current business model of a few large companies ahead of the clearly expressed wishes of the research and scientific sector as a whole.

Our message is simple: the forthcoming European Research Area (ERA) Act should include a Secondary Publication Right (SPR), which lets researchers share their work in an open repository.

title: Restauroitu Rauman raatihuone avautuu yleisölle 6.11.2026 – maailmanperintö ja historia esillä uusissa näyttelyissä
content:
Mittavan uudistuksen ja restauroinnin kokenut Rauman raatihuone (Kauppakatu 13) avataan yleisölle perjantaina 6.11.2026. Museokohteeseen on avajaispäivänä maksuton sisäänpääsy klo 12–17. Päivän aikana raatihuoneella voi tutustua uudistettuihin tiloihin, näyttelyihin ja museokauppaan juhlavan historiallisessa tunnelmassa.

Avajaispuhe pidetään klo 11.50, ja tämän jälkeen avajaisnauhan leikkaa Rauman museon ensimmäinen museonjohtaja Leena Rautavuori.

200 ensimmäiselle museovieraalle on tarjolla kahvia ja kakkua sisäpihalla. Avajaisissa esiintyy klo 13 muusikko Venla Wallenius. Yläkerran näyttelyyn järjestetään maksuttomat opastukset klo 14, 15 ja 16. Kuhunkin opastukseen mahtuu 15 henkilöä: paikat varataan hakemalla numerolappu museon asiakaspalvelupisteeltä klo 13 alkaen.

Ensimmäisestä kerroksesta löytyvä maailmanperinnön vierailukeskuksen näyttely esittelee Rauman molemmat UNESCOn maailmanperintökohteet, Vanhan Rauman ja Sammallahdenmäen pronssikautisen hautaröykkiöalueen. Lisäksi näyttelyssä kerrotaan maailmanperintösopimuksesta ja esitellään kaikki Suomen maailmanperintökohteet.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: Gulsuum osallistuu naisten Facebook-kapinointiin salaa veljiltään – ”Pienikin virhe voisi vaarantaa sekä oman että perheeni hengen”
content:
On varhainen aamu Afganistanin koillisosassa sijaitsevassa Parwanin maakunnassa. Ilmassa tuntuu aamun tuntien tyyneys, ja vain harvojen ohikulkijoiden askeleet rikkovat hiljaisuuden.

Erään kaupungin vaatimattomimpiin kuuluvissa kodeissa asuu 28-vuotias Gulsuum (nimi muutettu), joka elää oikeastaan kahta elämää.

Naapureidensa silmissä hän on hiljainen nuori nainen, joka käy ostamassa ruokaa, asuu perheensä luona ja yrittää elää tavallista arkea. Tämän julkisivun takana on kuitenkin ihminen, joka taistelee salanimen suojissa afganistanilaisnaisten koulutuksen, vapauden ja ihmisarvon puolesta.

Hän esiintyy nimellä Gulsuum suojatakseen henkilöllisyyttään. Hänen pelkonsa, toiveensa ja elämäntarinansa ovat kuitenkin täyttä totta.

Gulsuum asuu isänsä, äitinsä, tätinsä ja kahden veljensä kanssa yhdellä Parwanin maakunnan asuinalueista. Hänen naimaton tätinsä on pitkään ollut erottamaton osa perhettä.

Vain täti tietää Gulsuumin salaisuuden.

title: Scammers Are Stealing Millions From Food Stamp Recipients. Congress Could Fix It — but Won’t.
content:
It wasn’t the kind of call a grocery store gets every day. A customer with a thick Eastern European accent was on the phone saying he wanted to buy several thousand cans of Red Bull. Could the store have them in stock in a few days? Also, did they have equipment to move all those stacks of energy drinks into the parking lot, where two minivans would be waiting?

When the day came, Oct. 19, 2022, employees at the Smart & Final store in San Diego sold 3,960 cans of Red Bull and 720 of Monster Energy to two men and two women, all with the same accent, and helped them wheel the pallets out back. To pay for it all — the bill came to $10,747.05 — the group pulled out piles of plastic. These weren’t credit or debit cards; they looked more like hotel-room keys. There were 25 cards in all, each with a different amount loaded onto it, and the four people took turns swiping one after another. Then, the payment complete, they drove off.

title: Två nya böcker i serien Värt att veta: Sport och Feminism
content:
I höst utforskar vi brännande frågor om kamp, motstånd och rörelse genom sport och feminism. Heidi Kurvinen samt Antti Kuusela och Riitta-Ilona Pummi-Kuusela förmedlar stora insikter i kompakt format på 60 sidor.

I Sport tar Antti Kuusela och Riitta-Ilona Pummi-Kuusela pulsen på idrottens motsägelsefulla värld och väsen. Den är på många sätt primitiv – ett område för tävlan och kamp – men också en arena för ideal och drömmar där människor möts. Boken utforskar idrottens historia och myter, och ställer frågor om varför människor idrottar och vilken roll sporten spelar i våra liv.

– Alla kulturer har haft någon typ av sport och det finns inte ett enda område på jorden bebott av människor där man inte skulle känna till sport, säger författarna.

I Feminism visar Heidi Kurvinen på feminismens utveckling från historisk folkrörelse till dagens globala debatt. Under mer än hundra år har rörelsen varit en drivkraft för samhällsförändring, samtidigt som den mött motstånd. Boken belyser hur synen på kön, makt och ojämlikhet har förändrats över tid och hur dagens feminism både vinner ny mark och väcker starka reaktioner.

title: Kokeilussa uusi työkalu, joka pureutuu pikseleihin ja paljastaa peukaloinnin
content:
Maallikon silmään kuva on kuva. Konepellin alla se on kuitenkin bittejä, joiden avulla kuvatiedosto voidaan yksilöidä ja tarkistaa. Kansallisarkiston kehittämä Tarkista kuva -työkalu perustuu kahteen tekniseen ominaisuuteen: tiivisteeseen ja digitaaliseen vesileimaan.

Tarkista kuva on selainpohjainen työkalu, joka koostuu kahdesta osasta: taustalla olevasta tarkistusrekisteristä ja käyttäjälle näkyvästä tarkistustoiminnosta. Tarkistusrekisteriin arkisto tallentaa tietoa kuvista: tiivisteet ja vesileimojen tunnisteita aikaleimattuina. Aikaleima osoittaa, että nämä tiedot ovat olleet olemassa tietyllä hetkellä.

Tiiviste on tavallaan tiedoston sormenjälki. Se on algoritmilla tiedoston bittien perusteella laskettu, käytännössä yksilöllinen merkkijono. Jos tiedostosta muuttuu yksikin bitti, esimerkiksi yksi pikseli, tiivistekin muuttuu.

Digitaalinen vesileima taas on kuvan pikselidataan upotettu näkymätön tunniste. Vesileiman avulla kuva voidaan tunnistaa arkiston aineistoksi myös silloin, kun sitä on kevyesti muokattu.

title: Englannin vihreä vallankumous lässähti
content:
Kalle Pusa

Verde pohti keväällä, kuinka korkealle Englannin, ja Walesin, vihreiden liito saattaisi yltää. Vastaus on nyt saatu. 

Ei kovin korkealle. Kevään orastava vihreä vallankumous näyttää kellastuneen syksyn sateisiin. 

Torstaina 8. lokakuuta käytiin Holborn and St. Pancrasin vaalipiirin täytevaalit, joissa Englannin vihreiden puheenjohtaja Zack Polanski hävisi Britannian työväenpuolueen eli labourin Sagal Abdi-Walille selvin lukemin. Abdi-Wali sai 12 292 ääntä, kun taas Polanski keräsi 8 928 ääntä. 

Holbornin ja St. Pancrasin vaalipiiri on ollut vuosikymmeniä labour-puolueen ydinalueita Lontoossa. Polanskin mahdollisuuksia pidettiin matalina, kun hän asettui ehdolle, mutta syksyn tapahtumat romahduttivat pienenkin toivon voitosta. 

Pääministeri Andy Burnhamin työväenpuolue voi nyt huokaista helpotuksesta. Vaaleja pidettiin testinä siitä, kuinka suosittu Burnhamin valtakausi on ollut ja kuinka paljon keväällä nousussa ollut vihreät voisi labouria haastaa.

title: Character.ai's Bankruptcy Documents Show the Economics of AI Don't Work
content:
Character.ai’s bankruptcy is the one of the first dominos to fall in the long-foreseen AI bubble. The circumstances of its bankruptcy are exactly what critics of AI have been saying would happen: Character.ai lit a huge amount of money on fire running its product, did not bring in a lot of revenue, and faced enormous legal fees after causing harm to its users. Enshittifying its product to try to make its expenses cheaper did not work, according to a narrative filed in bankruptcy court Tuesday.

Disney has reportedly offered Character.ai $20 million to license some of its intellectual property; Last year, Disney sent Character.ai a cease and desist letter demanding it stop using its copyrighted characters without permission. In 2023, it was valued at $1 billion after raising $150 million in a round led by a16z.

title: Washington Could Defuse Europe’s “Kill Switch” Fears
content:
When the US Commerce department issued a directive requiring AI leader Anthropic to cut access to its Fable and Mythos models for all foreign nationals, Europeans feared the worst about Washington’s power to fire a “kill switch.” 

In reality, their fears were overblown. The shutoff represented a kneejerk response to an alleged jailbreak, using the only tool available to the administration: export controls. If the White House wanted to coerce its allies, it has other, less self-destructive ways to do so than ordering its most profitable companies to shut off their services. 

Despite this, a counterproductive kill switch meme drives European policy debate. US policy that imposed export controls on AI chips under both the Biden and Trump administrations has fueled support to de-risk from the US. Europe’s kill switch fear jeopardizes Washington’s vision of a US-led global AI stack to counter China. The US could and should reassure Europeans by guaranteeing access to US AI technology.

title: "Musk": Alex Gibney on New Film, Legal Threats & Elon Musk Spending $366M to Help GOP in Midterms
content:
We speak with the Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney about his new documentary Musk, an expansive, nearly four-hour examination of the world’s first trillionaire and how he has amassed unprecedented power in business, technology and politics. The film traces Elon Musk’s early ventures and the rise of SpaceX and Tesla, examining the role of government support in their growth. It also explores his acquisition of Twitter, now X; his alliance with President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement; and his role in the Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, whose cuts devastated federal programs, including USAID.

Gibney says Musk has carefully crafted an image of a “polymath” who can solve the world’s most pressing problems, but that he is really “kind of a ruthless businessman” willing to do whatever it takes to succeed, including “a series of elaborate cons” to win government support for his companies.

title: EU enlargement: Could new members face 15 years of oversight?
content:
The European Commission has presented MEPs with proposals to prepare the EU for a larger membership. The package sets out five areas for reform, from limiting national veto powers and expanding gradual integration to introducing safeguards designed to “hit hard” against countries that breach EU rules after joining. Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos argues that new members will not weaken the bloc but help make it fit for the future.

Presenting the Commission’s enlargement package in Strasbourg on 6 October, Kos described it as an “insurance policy” against democratic backsliding following enlargement. The package proposes a time-limited system of safeguards that would subject new member states to special oversight for up to 15 years after accession.

In cases of serious breaches of EU values, the mechanism could allow a country’s voting rights in the Council of the EU to be suspended. Kos said such protections were necessary to “protect ourselves”, pointing to “lessons from previous enlargements”.

For Kos, enlargement is not simply about bringing more countries into the EU. It is also an opportunity to make the Union stronger, more flexible and better equipped to take decisions.

title: As Federal Court Rules ALPRs are Mass Surveillance, EFF Gets Disappointing Ruling
content:
In an extremely disappointing ruling, a California trial court dismissed SIREN v. San Jose, our case challenging the city of San Jose’s warrantless searches of its vast stores of automated license plate reader (ALPR) data. EFF and the ACLU of Northern California represent SIREN and CAIR California, two non-profits that serve San Jose residents, in this case.

Make no mistake: We believe this ruling is wrong on the law, and we will appeal. The ruling ignores the importance of landmark rulings from the U.S. Supreme Court regarding the invasiveness of aggregating collected data on an individual over time, including one issued just months ago. It also severely underestimates the harm that ALPRs cause, in San Jose and around the country.

title: Report on the Execution of Four Prisoners in Tabriz Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, four prisoners were executed in Tabriz Central Prison on the morning of Wednesday, September 30, 2026.

The prisoners have been identified as Milad Safari, 39, a father of two; Ebrahim Khazali; Ahmadreza Zivari, 47; and Sadegh Hatami, 41.

According to the report, Milad Safari and Ebrahim Khazali had been sentenced to death in separate murder cases. Mr. Safari, a father of two, had been in detention for five years, while Mr. Khazali had been held for eight years.

Additionally, Ahmadreza Zivari and Sadegh Hatami had been sentenced to death in separate cases involving drug-related offenses. Before his arrest approximately two years ago, Mr. Zivari worked as a passenger driver. Mr. Hatami worked as a school transport driver for children before his arrest and had been imprisoned for approximately four years.

As of the time of this report, the executions have not been officially announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

title: Saudi Arabia: Death Penalty for Facebook Comment
content:
(Beirut) – A Saudi court has sentenced a Sri Lankan migrant worker to death over a Facebook comment that was deemed blasphemous, Human Rights Watch said today. Saudi authorities should reverse the judgment and release him immediately.

The Saudi Court of Appeal in the Eastern Region handed down the death sentence to Anojan Sivarasa, 24, on September 17, 2026, after two court sessions. An initial ruling had sentenced him to five years in prison.

“Sentencing a migrant worker to death over a Facebook comment that he has publicly apologized for is an outrageous overreaction from Saudi authorities amid a surge in executions,” said Joey Shea, senior Saudi Arabia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “No one should face execution for a comment on religion.”

title: FOI reform in Germany and Mexico
content:
Dear friend,

We can’t take our Freedom of Information laws for granted — as we’ve seen through the years with governmental pushback both in the UK, and in countless countries around the world.

In this free webinar, we’ll hear from those at the frontline of defending the right to know in Germany and Mexico, two countries where recent changes have raised important questions about the future of Access to Information.

In Germany, FragDenStaat say that they are facing "the most serious attack on transparency in the history of the Federal Republic and a threat to our democracy", with a proposed scrapping of ATI. In Mexico, a change in the agency responsible for FOI has undermined public access to information, ruling against most requests.

We hope you’ll join us on Oct 26 to hear these fascinating stories, and what civil society is doing to kick back against such challenges: find out more and book here.

Veza is Strategic Campaigner at FragDenStaat (Ask the State) in Germany.

Like mySociety's WhatDoTheyKnow, FragDenStaat provides a simple way for citizens to submit FOI requests online; and they also campaign very actively around information rights.

title: An Inside Look At How To Tame Unstoppable AI
content:
Earlier this year, a university decided to audit the effectiveness of its new AI system designed to help answer student questions. So, university officials hired me, an AI auditor, to come take a look. During my review, I discovered that the AI agent, which was supposed to handle only general questions about the academic calendar and organizational matters, had started opening students’ personal records — accessing data that wasn’t needed to answer their questions. The chatbot, however, did nothing further with that information.

When the university’s engineers, at the time, learned what happened from the access logs, they fixed it, and that was that. There was no official record. No internal rule required them to record such incidents, and nobody was assigned to track events like this. It was simply part of the engineering team’s bug-fixing process. The incident was what I call a near miss, and near misses are what a reporting system exists to catch. The same behavior could lead to something more serious next time, and we only know about this case because the university voluntarily brought me in to examine the system.

title: Hackers Turn French Supermarket Refrigerators Into Furnaces
content:
A massive cyberattack targeted hundreds of French supermarkets overnight on October 11 to 12, remotely hijacking refrigeration systems to trigger intense defrost cycles, spoiling vast quantities of food and sparking fires.

The unprecedented incident has triggered a national criminal investigation. The Paris Prosecutor's Office confirmed to OCCRP Tuesday that its cybercrime section has initiated an investigation, entrusted to the Anti-Cybercrime Office (OFAC). The probe aims to "identify the victims and establish a link between the incident and the damage reported by them, specifically regarding food spoilage and the outbreak of fires."

Hackers gained remote control of the store refrigeration systems by exploiting internet-connected controllers. The attack methodology mirrors vulnerabilities the operational technology security firm Claroty warned the industry about two months prior. In a prescient August report titled "Freeze the Controller, Defrost the Food," the firm's Team82 research division warned about the possibility that hackers could access Danfoss refrigeration systems to bypass security and manipulate temperatures.

title: The Names of Nearly 4 Million Enslaved People in Former British Colonies Are Now Searchable Online, Helping Descendants Find Lost Ancestors
content:
A few years ago, we featured here on Open Culture the Freedmen’s Bureau Project database, which contains searchable information on formerly enslaved people in the United States after its Civil War. With nearly 1.8 million men, women, and children registered there when it first opened to the public, it has remained a valuable resource for many Americans researching their own heritage, not just descendants of former slaves but of other Civil War refugees as well. But of course, the U.S. was hardly the only country where slavery existed. Countless people here in the twenty-first century have ancestors who were enslaved in other former British colonies, and now they’ve got a portal through which to do genealogical searches of their own.

Launched by a partnership between the genealogy company Ancestry and the Centre for the Study of the Legacies of British Slavery at University College London, the online Former British Colonies Enslavement Registers makes available records on nearly four million individuals enslaved between 1813 and 1840 in a host of countries from the Bahamas to Mauritius to South Africa.

title: Vieraskynä: Kun piiloon jäävä todellisuus tuodaan museoon
content:
Kulttuuripalvelujen käyttäminen ei useinkaan ole ensimmäisenä mielessä ihmisellä, joka elää asunnottomana tai muussa vakavassa asumisen kriisissä. Huomio suuntautuu siihen, miten arjen välttämättömät tarpeet järjestyvät ja mistä saa apua.

Museoon menemistä voivat rajoittaa pääsymaksujen lisäksi monet näkymättömämmät kynnykset. Museo saattaa tuntua vieraalta paikalta, ja osallistumista voivat vaikeuttaa asunnottomuuteen liittyvä stigma, häpeän kokemukset, kuormittava elämäntilanne sekä tunne siitä, ettei museo ole tarkoitettu “minunlaisilleni” ihmisille.

Siksi kulttuuripalvelujen saavutettavuus ei ole asunnottomuutta kokevien ihmisten näkökulmasta toissijainen kysymys. Se kertoo siitä, ketkä tunnistetaan yhteiskunnan täysivaltaisiksi jäseniksi ja keiden kokemusten katsotaan kuuluvan yhteiseen kulttuuriin ja historiaan.

Yhteistyömme esimerkiksi Arkkitehtuuri- ja designmuseon kanssa on ollut merkityksellistä. Siihen on kuulunut asiantuntijuuden vaihtoa, Arkkitehtuuri kuuluu kaikille -podcastin sisällöntuotantoa ja 2 139 -installaation eli origamitaloista koostuvan yhteisötaideteoksen rakentamista museon aulaan.

title: Kaipuu energiaomavaraisuuteen voi lisätä ilmastotoimien kannatusta
content:
Geopoliittiset jännitteet vaikuttavat myös Suomessa julkiseen keskusteluun energia- ja ilmastopolitiikasta. Ilmastotoimien kannalta on tärkeää edistää eri ryhmien yhteistä ymmärrystä niiden hyödyistä.

Vaikka enemmistö maailman ihmisistä kannattaa ilmastotoimia, niiden säätäminen ja käyttöönotto on usein poliittisesti vaikeaa. Samalla kun ilmastonmuutoksen monet negatiiviset vaikutukset jakautuvat maapallolla epätasaisesti, myöskään ilmastotoimien vaikutukset eivät ole yhtäläiset.

Kaikki toki hyötyvät pitkällä tähtäimellä elinvoimaisesta ja -kelpoisesta planeetasta. Kuitenkin lyhyellä aikavälillä toimet saattavat luoda häviäjiä – niitä, joille politiikkatoimista koituu maksuja, ansionmenetyksiä tai muuta haitallista. Samalla toinen osa saattaa taloudellisesti suuresti hyötyä ilmastotoimista. Monet poliitikot ja puolueet ovat käyttäneet hyödykseen ilmastotoimien häviäjien epävarmuutta ja tyytymättömyyttä.

title: Celebrating five years of strengthening open digital infrastructure
content:
Five years after the feasibility study for investing in the infrastructure of the 21st century, we look back and ahead: how do we strengthen the open source foundation of the future?

Five years ago, the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWi) commissioned a small team to work out, in a feasibility study, how public investment in open digital infrastructure could be designed. In late 2021, the Log4Shell vulnerability in Apache Log4j, a widely used open source software library, caused far-reaching damage. Log4j was running in millions of systems at the time, and the vulnerability spread along software dependencies into public administration systems and critical infrastructure worldwide. The incident exposed a dire situation hiding in plain sight. Open source technologies, from programming libraries and protocols to developer tools and software components, form the technical foundation of all modern digital systems. Yet they suffer from chronic underinvestment, and they are developed and maintained mostly by volunteers. Countless people, companies, and institutions depend on them, but few invest in maintaining them.

title: Suomen kirjastoseuran hallitusohjelmatavoitteet 2027-2031
content:
Kirjastoseura on julkaissut hallitusohjelmatavoitteensa vuosille 2027-2031.

  • Kirjastot osaksi kansallista lukutaito- ja oppimispolitiikkaa

    • Suomen heikentyneet PISA-tulokset osoittavat, että lukutaidon vahvistaminen on kansallinen tehtävä. Kirjastot tulee tunnistaa vahvemmin osaksi oppimisen ekosysteemiä yhdessä varhaiskasvatuksen, koulujen, oppilaitosten ja kotien kanssa. 

    Kirjasto on tärkeä lukutaito- ja oppimisympäristö yhteiskunnassa. Se tukee lukemista, tiedonhakua, medialukutaitoa ja elinikäistä oppimista kaikenikäisille suomalaisille. 

  • Resursseja kuntien lukutaitotyöhön

    • Valtion tulee tukea kuntien lukutaito-ohjelmien toteuttamista pitkäjänteisesti. Opetushallituksen kansalliset tavoitteet on saatava näkyviksi myös paikallisella tasolla siten, että kunnilla on käytettävissään riittävät resurssit lukemisen edistämiseen. 

    Kirjastot ovat luonteva ja kustannustehokas kumppani kuntien lukutaitotyössä. Niiden osaamista tulee hyödyntää järjestelmällisesti osana kuntien sivistys- ja hyvinvointipolitiikkaa. 

  • Jokaisella lapsella ja nuorella on oltava pääsy kirjastopalveluihin

title: OpenAI employee arrested and charged over hidden recording
content:
Federal authorities arrested a Saudi national employed at OpenAI and charged him with planting a recording device in a company’s executive conference room, the Department of Justice announced Tuesday.

On or around Sept. 30, OpenAI discovered a sophisticated recording device inserted into the back of a television in an executive conference room located in one of its San Francisco offices. The company determined that the device was installed approximately a couple days prior, concealed in toilet paper. The contents of the device were encrypted, according to the DOJ.

The Department of Justice said in a news release that the employee, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was arrested Friday and appeared in federal court Tuesday. OpenAI confirmed the incident on social media and said that it was supporting the FBI’s investigation.

“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier,” OpenAI said in its statement. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data.”

title: Trainees explore Community Engagement
content:
How can heritage practitioners create meaningful opportunities for communities to shape the ways their heritage is understood, cared for and shared? This question guided HERITΛGE’s recent four-day online workshop, Engaging Communities in Cultural Heritage, which brought together 23 participants from 18 countries.

Participants joined from Poland, Lebanon, Italy, Iraq, Albania, Greece, Armenia, Rwanda, Serbia, Latvia, Mauritius, India, Egypt, Iran, South Africa, Kenya, Palestine and Nepal to explore 

The programme examined different understandings of community, identity, belonging and relationships with heritage, while emphasising the importance of positionality, research, inclusion, accessibility and meaningful participation. 

Participants were introduced to approaches including Asset-Based Community Development, asset mapping and ethnographic research, exploring how community assets, knowledge, relationships and networks can inform the design and implementation of engagement activities.

title: Ny på jobbet: projektledare för samverkansprojektet Ett Wikispeech för alla
content:
Wikimedia Sverige välkomnar Amelia Högberg som i augusti av 2026 har börjat hos oss i rollen som projektledare för samverkansprojektet Ett Wikispeech för alla. Nedan följer en kort presentation:

Jag heter Amelia Högberg och började på Wikimedia Sverige i augusti 2026 som projektledare för samverkansprojektet Ett Wikispeech för alla. Projektet syftar till att öka tillgängligheten på Wikimedias plattformar för fler målgrupper genom utvecklandet av en talsyntes med öppen källkod.  

Jag har en bakgrund inom humaniora, kultur och teknik blandat med vetenskap och innovation, och har en magisterexamen i filosofi. En allt starkare drivkraft hos mig har varit att bidra till att humanistiska och etiska perspektiv får ta större plats i teknikutvecklingen, och det var en av anledningarna till att jag sökte mig till Wikimedia. Innan jag kom hit jobbade jag för AI Swedens språkteknologiska grupp, där mitt fokus bland annat var att sprida gruppens forskningsresultat inom storskaliga språkmodeller med öppen källkod och att samverka med partners och intressenter.

title: The Zine Atlas
content:
The following is a guest post by the 2025-2026 Innovator in Residence, Vivian Li. As part of her work with the Library, Vivian hosted a series of community outreach events, including zine-making workshops in partnership with the Chicago Public Library. Read on to learn how you can also make a zine and check out the end of the post to print your own copy of research zines created by Vivan about various LOC collections.

In Chicago, the Anywhere Adventures team ran a series of workshops inviting people to make zines about their neighborhood. These zines could describe a piece of history that happened on your block, a memory you have, some kind of guide, or anything you want to share and preserve about your piece of the world.

I’ve been copying and gathering these zines into a community artbook called the Zine Atlas. If you would like to make a zine and contribute it to the Atlas, or if you just want to participate in the writing prompts we used in Chicago, you can do it yourself at home!

Materials needed:
– Paper (2 sheets)
– Scissors
– Drawing supplies (just a pencil/pen is fine, but feel free to use anything!)

title: India: Joint submission to GANHRI regarding review of the accreditation status of the National Human Rights Commission of India
content:
We, the undersigned, are regional and international human rights nongovernmental organizations as well as individuals expressing concerns over the developments at the National Human Rights Commission of India (NHRCI). 

The submitting organizations have varying degrees of direct work with the NHRCI. Most of us have been involved in advocacy to push for the NHRCI’s compliance with the United Nations Principles relating to the Status of National Institutions (The Paris Principles). We have repeatedly made submissions to the Sub-Committee on Accreditation (SCA) concerning the accreditation of NHRCI in 2023, 2024, 2025, most recently in March 2026 and now in this “Alteration of Accreditation.” 

In March 2025, the GANHRI-SCA recommended downgrading NHRCI’s accreditation and gave it one year before making a final decision. The SCA recommended that the NHRCI improve its processes and functions in line with the Paris Principles. The NHRCI challenged the downgrade before GANHRI but it was rejected in December 2025, and the NHRCI’s “Alteration of Accreditation” review was postponed from March to November 2026.

title: Mediat: Google pyytää anteeksi hakkuusotkujaan
content:
Teknologiajätti Googlen Suomen-maajohtaja Antti Järvinen pyytää anteeksi yhtiön Muhoksella ja Kajaanissa datakeskustyömailla tekemiä metsähakkuita.

Järvinen myöntää Ylelle, Helsingin Sanomille ja MTV:n uutisille antamissaan haastatteluissa, että yhtiö on tehnyt hankkeissa virheitä. Tätä ennen hän ei juuri ole antanut haastatteluja medialle hakkuuasiasta.

Yhtiön edustajia on muutenkin ollut vaikea tavoittaa kommentoimaan sotkua.

- Olen erittäin pahoillani, että ollaan tässä tilanteessa. Haluan sitä pyytää anteeksi, Järvinen sanoo Ylelle.

MTV:n uutisille Järvinen sanoo, että yhtiö kantaa vastuun tapahtuneesta.

- Olemme tehneet päätökset meidän parhaan käsityksemme mukaan vallitsevasta lainsäädännöstä. Vain ja ainoastaan me kannamme siitä vastuun. Tällä hetkellä tärkeintä on se, että pääsisimme tästä erittäin rakentavasti ja hyvässä yhteistyössä eteenpäin, Järvinen sanoo MTV:n uutisille.

GOOGLEN suomalainen tytäryhtiö hakkautti datakeskusten työmailla puustoa ja teetti maansiirtotöitä, vaikka hankkeiden ympäristövaikutusten arviointimenettely oli kesken.

Lupa- ja valvontavirasto eli LVV on todennut hakkuiden vaativan yva-menettelyn ja kehottanut keskeyttämään datakeskusten valmistelutyöt.

title: Bringing Wiki Projects to the 2026 Summer Institute in Computational Social Science in Kenya
content:
Wait, you can just access all that knowledge and even contribute to it?!

A SICSS participant when learning about Wikimedia projects

Wait, you can just access all that knowledge and even contribute to it?!

A SICSS participant when learning about Wikimedia projects

It takes a village of people with different skills to create, maintain and learn from open knowledge. And the 2026 edition of the Kenyan Summer Institute in Computational Social Science (SICSS) offered just the place for that, by bringing together social scientists, technologists, and Wikimedians to learn from each other.

Since 2017, the SICSS events bring together scholars in computational social science in different locations around the world for two intense weeks of project-based learning, in which early career researchers are trained in computational methods during the first week. Those newly learned skills are then directly applied to concrete, co-designed group research projects during the second week. And in many cases continue onwards beyond the project window.

title: Poetry book promotes Chabacano, Asia’s only Spanish-based creole language
content:
Ten authors and 23 poems are featured in the anthology

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo from the Facebook page of Voces del Alma. Used with permission

A new poetry anthology features writers of Chabacano, one of the Philippines’ 170 languages, which is widely spoken in the southernmost city of Zamboanga, and stands out as Asia’s only Spanish-based creole language.

The Philippines was a colony of Spain for more than three centuries, but the Spanish language was only used by the elite, friars, and colonial rulers. Only in Zamboanga did a Spanish-based creole language develop.

In 2018, Global Voices featured Bien Chabacano, a blog dedicated to promoting and documenting Chavacano de Zamboanga. Its creator, Jerome Herrera, launched a book project this year by inviting writers to submit poems to be compiled in an anthology. This led to the launch of the “Sombra y Luz” book in July, featuring 23 poems by 10 authors. The poems are mainly about love, family, and Zamboangueño identity.

title: Ensimmäinen kattava tietokirja suomalaisen avangarden suuresta ulkopuolisesta, J. O. Mallanderista
content:
J. O. Mallander esitteli kansainvälisen nykytaiteen uusimpia virtauksia muun muassa Hufvudstadsbladetissa ja Taide-lehdessä. Hän toimi Dagens Nyheterin taidekriitikkona ja kirjoitti myös moniin ruotsalaisiin taidelehtiin. Mallander johti 1970-luvun alussa perustettua Elonkorjaajat-taiteilijaryhmää ja samalla vuosikymmenellä toiminutta Halvat Huvit -galleriaa, joka esitteli tuohon aikaan muodikkaan yhteiskunnallisen realismin vastapainona käsitetaidetta, minimalismia, videotaidetta, valokuvataidetta, installaatioita, postitaidetta ja sarjakuvataidetta.

Teoksen kirjoittaja Marko Home (1963–2025) oli taidehistoriasta väitellyt filosofian tohtori, jonka erikoisalaa oli kansainvälinen ja kotimainen avantgardetaide. Postuumisti julkaistava teos on ensimmäinen kokonaisesitys J. O. Mallanderin toiminnasta taidekentällä. Kirjan esipuheen on kirjoittanut taidehistorian emeritusprofessori Ville Lukkarinen.

title: He Waited Nine Years in Prison for His Lawyer to File a Single Brief. In This State, There’s No Rule Against It.
content:
In 2020, seven years after he was appointed to represent a client who claimed he was wrongly convicted, attorney Scott Galloway told the judge that he was still looking into the case and needed more time.  

“I am still in the process of interviewing individuals,” the lawyer wrote to the judge in Delaware County, outside Philadelphia, who had already granted him 32 extensions. 

His client, Nolan O’Neal, had been a 20-year-old high school student when he was arrested for murder by Chester police, who had four eyewitnesses identifying him. At his 2005 trial, those witnesses all recanted, saying police had pressured them to accuse O’Neal. 

By the time Galloway joined the case, in 2013, O’Neal had already spent eight years in prison insisting he was innocent. The lawyer’s job was to help him file a petition under Pennsylvania’s Post Conviction Relief Act. That law provided a narrow path to freedom if Galloway could find crucial new evidence or prove that previous lawyers had mishandled the case.

But court records do not show that the attorney did much other than ask for more time.

title: Försök med ett nytt verktyg som granskar pixlar och avslöjar manipulationer
content:
För en lekman är en bild en bild. Under ytan handlar det ändå om bitar som gör det möjligt att identifiera och kontrollera en bildfil. Verktyget Kontrollera bild som har tagits fram av Riksarkivet bygger på två tekniska funktioner: hashvärde och digital vattenstämpel.

Kontrollera bild är ett webbläsarbaserat verktyg som består av två delar: ett kontrollregister i bakgrunden och en kontrollfunktion som visas för användaren. Kontrollregistret arkiverar information om bilder: tidsstämplade identifierare för hashvärden och vattenstämplar. Tidsstämpeln visar att dessa uppgifter har funnits vid en viss tidpunkt.

Hashvärdet är på sätt och vis filens fingeravtryck. Det är en i praktiken unik sträng som har beräknats utifrån filens bitar med en algoritm. Om bara en enda bit i filen ändras, till exempel en pixel, förändras också hashvärdet.

En digital vattenstämpel är däremot en osynlig identifierare som bäddats in i bildens pixeldata. Med hjälp av vattenstämpeln kan en bild identifieras som arkivmaterial även när den har redigerats lätt.

title: LekaMed continues – Focus on democratic education, participation and agency
content:
How can adults and children together create a more democratic everyday environment in early childhood education and pre-primary education? is one of the questions explored during the project this autumn. Throughout the autumn, Marina and Sara are working closely with a pre-primary education group and its staff to explore this and related questions. 

Alongside the collection of research data, staff are supported in their professional development in matters related to democratic education, participation, and agency. Material developed in collaboration with Petra Holm at Moilo is being tested together with staff in the group, while different approaches to creating a more democracy-promoting everyday environment are also being explored. 

Through this collaboration, we aim to develop approaches and practices that can be shared with other professionals working in early childhood education. The goal is to contribute to a culture in which children can experience democracy and where children’s voices are given genuine space and taken seriously, says Marina.

title: Mepit vaativat EU:lta arvopohjaista Kiina-politiikkaa
content:
Euroopan parlamentti haluaa, että EU pitää Kiina-politiikassa kiinni arvoistaan, jotka liittyvät muun muassa ihmisoikeuksiin, ilmastoon, kauppaan ja turvallisuuteen. Viime viikolla hyväksytyssä suosituksessa mepit toteavat, että monikeskeisen maailmanjärjestyksen edistäminen on EU:n edun mukaista. Kiinan kanssa olisi tärkeää käydä vuoropuhelua globaaleista haasteista.

Euroopan parlamentin ja Kiinan hallituksen kontaktit olivat jäissä neljä vuotta, aina kevääseen 2025 saakka, jolloin osapuolet alkoivat purkaa rajoituksia. Syynä olivat EU:n ihmisoikeussyistä asettamat Kiina-pakotteet, minkä seurauksena Kiina asetti useita europarlaamentikkoja perheineen maahantulokieltoon.

Tänä vuonna välit ovat lämmenneet, ja jo useita Euroopan parlamentin valtuuskuntia on vieraillut Kiinassa.

Uudessa suosituksessa kuitenkin todetaan, että EU:n suhteet Kiinaan ovat kriittisessä tilassa johtuen Kiinan epäreilusta talouspolitiikasta ja kannasta Venäjän Ukrainassa käymään sotaan.

title: Ukraine Has Problems With Both Koreas
content:
When South Korean President Lee Jae-myung lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over a prisoner-of-war transfer in September, the reaction blindsided many and raised questions about why Seoul was escalating what seemed like a relatively minor diplomatic dispute.

Ukraine had captured the two North Korean soldiers fighting for Russia, and both reportedly wanted to go to South Korea. Kyiv eventually transferred them to Seoul, but when Zelenskyy mentioned the transfer during his speech at the United Nations, Lee publicly objected.

South Korea said the transfer was supposed to remain secret, while Ukraine said there was no nondisclosure agreement. Lee accused Kyiv of effectively “branding the head of state of the other country a liar” and warned that South Korea could take additional measures against Ukraine. Seoul did not let the matter drop. It recalled its ambassador from Kyiv.

No doubt Zelenskyy’s revelation was embarrassing to the South Koreans (the news provoked some criticism inside the country for a supposed appeasement of North Korea), but the reaction seemed overblown.

title: Yemen Plunges Back into "Full-Scale Civil War," Houthis Trade Strikes with Saudi Arabia
content:
Yemen’s Ansar Allah, also known as the Houthis, have repeatedly attacked the Saudi capital of Riyadh in recent days. On Saturday, a missile strike on the airport in Riyadh killed at least 12 and injured over 300 in the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in over a decade. President Trump is now weighing whether to join the Saudi fight against the Houthis in Yemen.

This latest escalation comes after Ansar Allah captured key areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in recent weeks, driving back the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government and taking control of the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

“Yes, the Houthis are attacking Saudi Arabia with airstrikes, but there is now, actively, a real ground war going on within Yemen, and that is a far more relevant and important issue for the Yemenis on a day-to-day basis because they are now back into a full-scale civil war,” says Middle East scholar Helen Lackner.

title: Will the UK rejoin the EU? Andy Burnham’s plan has two goals, expert says
content:
Until recently, the British government was reluctant to entertain the possibility of rejoining the European Union. Now, London’s position appears to be shifting. At the Labour Party’s annual conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for a debate on the future of Britain’s relationship with the EU.

“Brexit has done more harm than good,” Burnham said. He outlined several possible paths forward: maintaining the current relationship, joining the EU customs union, returning to the single market or even becoming a full member of the bloc again. On the last option, he suggested Britain could go “all the way”.

Burnham has stressed, however, that rejoining the EU remains a distant prospect. He has also suggested that another referendum might not necessarily be required.

According to Krzysztof Winkler, an analyst at the Warsaw Enterprise Institute, a Polish economic policy think tank, the prime minister’s position reflects both economic and political considerations.

“Western societies are now deeply divided between liberal-left and conservative camps. Essentially, we’re dealing with two very different ways of looking at the world,” Winkler explains.

title: Privacy's Defenders Podcast: No Privacy Without Encryption
content:
When we communicate online today – from your personal emails and DMs to secure international commerce – we usually do so with encryption. Encryption converts readable data into unreadable gibberish to protect our privacy and security. This didn’t just happen organically. Three decades ago, the U.S government treated encryption like a weapon, and it took some unlikely heroes to set it free: a grad student, a junior lawyer, and a fledgling digital rights group who sued the federal government. 

The ruling in Bernstein v. Department of Justice held that code is speech and so is protected by the First Amendment – a precedent that underpins the internet as we know it today. This landmark case was led by Cindy Cohn, then a young pro bono lawyer working on behalf of EFF, who went on to become EFF’s legal director and then executive director. 

Welcome to the second episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was. 

(You can also find this episode on the Internet Archive and on YouTube.)

title: Death Sentence of Amirhassan Akbari-Monfared Upheld by Supreme Court
content:
According to HRANA, Branch 41 of the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence of political prisoner Amirhassan Akbari-Monfared and communicated to him in prison on October 11, 2026. In July of this year, he was sentenced to death by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, on charges of baghi (armed rebellion) through membership in the People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran (PMOI/MEK).

Amirhassan Akbari-Monfared was arrested alongside his father, Mohammad Akbari-Monfared, his brother Amirhossein, and his sister Zeinab by Ministry of Intelligence agents in Karaj during the winter of 2025. Some time later, three members of his family were released on bail.

No information has yet been obtained regarding the specific charges brought against the other members of his family. However, a source familiar with the situation of these political defendants previously told HRANA that they were facing security-related charges.

Mohammad Akbari-Monfared, aged approximately 58, Amirhossein Akbari-Monfared, 33, Zeinab Akbari-Monfared, 30, and Amirhassan Akbari-Monfared are all residents of Karaj.

title: France Shouldn’t Return Afghans to Taliban Rule
content:
France has confirmed that it has opened a “technical dialogue” with the Taliban authorities regarding forced returns to Afghanistan. The announcement marks a dangerous shift in policy that places Afghans in France at risk of persecution, torture and other grave abuses in contravention of France’s international human rights obligations.

The “technical dialogue” follows in the wake of a Taliban delegation to Brussels in June in which migration and return policies were discussed with European Union officials. Germany has already deported 263 Afghans since last year.

The French Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the talks aim “to facilitate the removal of Afghan nationals who are illegally on the national territory and who represent a national security risk.” French officials say the dialogue is narrowly focused but have not set out any guarantees that those at particular risk, including women, would be protected.

title: UK Sanctions Dutch Businessman Allegedly Linked to Russian Arms Firms
content:
The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions⁠ on Dutch businessman Alexander Tattersall and his Turkish company, Redwing Metal, following a joint investigation by The Kyiv Independent, OCCRP and IrpiMedia that exposed shipments of European industrial equipment to Russian factories supplying missile and fighter jet manufacturers.

Tattersall and Redwing Metal were among 38 individuals, companies and vessels targeted⁠ by the British government on October 8 as part of a broader effort to disrupt Russia’s military supply chains, oil revenues and financial networks.

The measures freeze assets under British jurisdiction and prohibit British individuals and businesses from conducting transactions with the designated parties.

The sanctions follow a June investigation⁠ by OCCRP, The Kyiv Independent and Italy’s IrpiMedia, which revealed that Redwing Metal had shipped more than $5 million worth of European-made industrial machinery to two Russian metallurgical plants in 2023 and 2024, despite EU export restrictions.

The equipment included computer-controlled lathes, metal heat-treatment furnaces, hydraulic presses and other machinery manufactured in Italy, Germany, Spain and the Czech Republic.

title: The Bialetti Moka Express: The History of Italy’s Iconic Coffee Maker, and How to Use It the Right Way
content:
I am sure that many an Open Culture reader has a Bialetti Moka Express in their kitchen. I know I do, but I must add that I knew little about its history and apparently even less about how to properly use one. Coffee expert and author of The World Atlas of Coffee James Hoffmann introduces us to the appliance we think we know in the above video.

Alfonso Bialetti didn’t originally get into the coffee business. In 1919, the Bialetti company was an aluminum manufacturer, with the Moka Express invented somewhere around 1933 by Luigi de Ponti, who worked for the company. According to Deconstructing Product Design by William Lidwell and Gerry Manacsa, the inspiration came from Bialetti’s wife’s old-fashioned washing machine: “a fire, a bucket, and a lid with a tube coming out of it. The bucket was filled with soapy water, sealed with the lid, and then brought to a boil over the fire, at which point the vaporized soapy water was pushed up through the tube and expelled on to the laundry.”

title: How Maroš Šefčovič talked his way to a China trade breakthrough
content:
Europe’s trade chief has won a first concession from Beijing. Now he must convince EU leaders that dialogue can deliver more.

By Camille Gijs and Carlo Martuscelli
in Brussels

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

When Maroš Šefčovič set out his strategy for engaging with China to European Union ambassadors in July, he had a warning for governments urging tougher action on trade against Beijing.

“Sometimes, it’s even popular to start a trade war, but it’s very difficult to finish it,” the EU trade chief recalled later in an interview with POLITICO.

Three months on, Šefčovič has secured a first breakthrough, reaching a deal in Beijing last week to sharply reduce imports of Chinese hybrid cars. The symbolic win marks a small step toward stabilizing a trading relationship that Brussels believes has reached a dangerous tipping point.

The agreement, which will initially cap imports at 350,000 vehicles a year, marks a significant concession from Beijing, whose carmakers have been flooding the European market with increasingly competitive vehicles.

title: Global: New report exposes human rights failures at 2026 Men’s World Cup
content:
Coalition calls for upcoming FIFA presidential election to centre human rights 

The 2026 Men’s World Cup exposed a failure of FIFA’s leadership to implement its own human rights policies, with the pursuit of record revenues prioritised over fairness and equality, the Sport & Rights Alliance and Football Supporters Europe said in a joint report released today. The 50-page report, “Profit Over People: The 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup,” documents a tournament marked by a climate of fear given the backdrop of mass immigration detentions and deportations; discriminatory visa bans; cost and accessibility barriers for fans, players and journalists; unclear safeguarding and eligibility standards; and lack of effective access to remedy.
snippet: Coalition calls for upcoming FIFA presidential election to centre human rights

title: Sikarutto etenee: uusia tautilöydöksiä Lappeenrannasta ja Pyhtäältä
content:
Afrikkalaista sikaruttoa on löytynyt Kaakkois-Suomesta aiemman ydinalueen ulkopuolelta, ja tauti näyttää Ruokaviraston mukaan edenneen.

Ruokaviraston tiedotteen mukaan Lappeenrannan luota, viitisen kil0metriä nykyisen ydinalueen ulkopuolelta, on ammuttu ruttoon sairastunut villisika.

Samoin Pyhtäältä ja Virolahdelta on löytynyt ruttoon kuolleiden sikojen luita ja ruhojäänteitä.

Kaikkiaan uusia tautilöydöksiä on tehty 15, ja virasto arvelee ruton levinneen aiempien alueiden ulkopuolelle. Virasto sanookin laajentavansa ydinaluetta lähipäivinä.

Virasto kertoo, että löydösalueilla jatketaan sikajäänteiden etsintää.

AFRIKKALAINEN sikarutto on sioille hengenvaarallinen virustauti, mutta se ei tartu ihmisiin eikä muihin eläimiin.

Suomessa ensimmäiset tautitapaukset havaittiin heinä-elokuun vaihteessa.

Ruokavirasto on määritellyt Itä-Suomesta yli 300 000 hehtaaria tartuntavyöhykkeeksi. Se tarkoittaa aluetta, jolta tautia on löydetty ja jossa on kohonnut taudin leviämisriski.

Ydinalue on kirjaimellisesti tartuntavyöhykkeen ytimessä oleva alue, jossa liikkujien täytyy muun muassa desinfioida jalkineensa ja kulkuneuvonsa.

title: Strengthening Language Communities in the Open Movement: Reflections from the Inaugural Language Diversity Conference
content:
From 2 to 4 October 2026, Accra, Ghana, became a gathering point for people working to preserve, document, strengthen, and advance the world’s linguistic diversity.

The inaugural Language Diversity Conference was held at Fiesta Royale Hotel under the theme “Strengthening Language Communities in the Open Movement.”

The conference was organized by the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group, in collaboration with Wikitongues, Wikimedia UK, and Language Diversity Hub, with funding from the Wikimedia Foundation.

Welcoming the global language community to Accra. Participants began arriving on 1 October from different parts of the world. As members of the local organizing team, we were responsible for welcoming participants and managing registration.

title: Kirjoja lainataan yhä enemmän – vuonna 2027 lainauskorvaus alimmalle tasolle kymmeneen vuoteen
content:
Suomalaiset lainaavat kirjastoista kirjoja yhä enemmän, mutta ensi vuonna lainauskorvauksiin käytettävissä oleva määräraha on entistä niukempi eikä se riitä pitämään korvausta edes nykyisellä tasolla. Sanaston laatiman ennusteen mukaan lainakohtainen korvaus laskee vuonna 2027 nykyisestä 25 sentistä 23 senttiin, ellei eduskunta lisää lainauskorvausmäärärahaa. Nykyisen, jo madaltuneen korvaustason säilyttäminen edellyttää 1,2 miljoonan euron lisärahoitusta.

Kirjastojen kasvavat lainamäärät ovat erinomainen uutinen lukemiselle ja lukutaidolle. Kirjallisuuden tekijöiden näkökulmasta tilanne on kuitenkin lohduton: mitä enemmän teoksia lainataan, sitä pienemmäksi yhdestä lainasta maksettava korvaus jää. Kolmessa vuodessa kirjallisuuden tekijöiden saamat korvaukset ovat laskeneet jo 20 prosenttia.

title: Apple unveils new smart home devices that showcase upgraded Siri AI
content:
New products from Apple include the HomeView, an iPad-like device that acts as a hub for other smart home gadgets

Apple on Tuesday began showing off a ⁠new round of smart home products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops ⁠and act as a hub for other smart home devices.

The HomeView device starts at $299 and will begin shipping next month. It will feature a 7in screen and face recognition, will help users ⁠control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. The device will also showcase Apple’s AI-upgraded Siri virtual ​assistant.

title: Metsäteollisuuden markkinat pysyvät vaisuina – ensi vuonna odotetaan maltillista kasvua
content:
Metsäteollisuustuotteiden kysyntä pysyy Suomen tärkeillä vientimarkkinoilla vaimeana, ennustaa Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) metsäsektorin suhdannekatsaus. Sahatavaran kysynnän odotetaan elpyvän hitaasti vuonna 2027, mutta kemiallisen metsäteollisuuden markkinatilanne säilyy vaisumpana. Puun hinnat laskevat tänä vuonna ja kääntyvät maltilliseen nousuun ensi vuonna.

Metsäteollisuuden toimintaympäristöä varjostavat hidas talouskasvu, kiristyvä kansainvälinen kilpailu ja geopoliittinen epävarmuus. Suomen metsäteollisuuden tuotanto kasvaa vuonna 2027 vain maltillisesti, ja kannattavuus jää hienoisesta kohenemisesta huolimatta vaatimattomaksi.

”Talouskasvun lievä vahvistuminen tukee kysyntää ensi vuonna, mutta nopeaa käännettä parempaan ei ole näköpiirissä. Markkinoilla on runsaasti kapasiteettia, ja kilpailu vientimarkkinoilla säilyy kireänä”, sanoo johtava tutkija Matleena Kniivilä.

title: The Creator of ‘Smutstep’ Wants You to ‘Let Your Freak Flag Fly’
content:
Last week, a video came across my feed of a man saying horny lines over a dubstep beat. “On your knees,” he snarled. As the beat dropped, he growled, “Mmm, now look at me.” 

“Instagram reels just showed me a guy who makes 'smutstep' for the booktok crowd and it is the funniest thing I have ever watched,” the person reposting the video on X wrote. The replies are predictably harsh: “I think this is actually the worst thing I have ever heard.” “Who the FUCK is demanding this 😭” 

People demanding this is why it exists. DARQ DAGR, whose real name is James, is a dubstep musician and voice artist who’s been working in the music industry and voice acting world for years. But smutstep is what’s made his work go viral, in part thanks to the people who hate it so much – and the ones who demand more of it.

title: Europe Can Rearm Even as Steel Industry Shrinks
content:
Total defense spending by EU states reached €418bn in 2025 (about $468bn), according to the European Defence Agency. Crude steel production fell to 125.8m tonnes, its lowest recorded level, says the industry association. Governments are asking arms manufacturers to expand while much of their industrial base struggles to remain profitable. This can be managed, but it requires some thought and care.

A construction-steel mill cannot simply switch to armor plate. Gun barrels require specialized metallurgy followed by advanced forging and machining. Naval components introduce different constraints, including the size of available equipment. ArcelorMittal’s specialist steel subsidiary Industeel uses vacuum treatment and controlled plate production for protection steels. Comparable chemistry alone does not make another supplier acceptable. Qualification takes time, and an idle furnace cannot clear a queue at a heat-treatment line.

title: Planetary diet in Polish schools sparks controversy: “The biggest problem is parents”
content:
It all started with a single dish made from beans or lentils. Before long, Poland was embroiled in a heated debate over hungry schoolchildren, digestive problems and claims of forced veganism. The trigger? A new government regulation changing what can be served in school canteens.

But first, what exactly is the planetary diet? Despite claims circulating online, it is not a Polish government initiative designed to take meat off children’s menus.

The term planetary health diet gained international attention in 2019, when the EAT-Lancet Commission, an international group of scientists, proposed a way of eating that would be healthier for people and less damaging to the environment.

It is not a vegan diet. Although largely plant-based, it allows for animal products, including dairy, poultry and fish. The emphasis is on eating more vegetables, fruit, whole grains, nuts and legumes, while consuming less red meat and sugar.

Which brings us to Polish schools — and the legumes that have become an unlikely source of national controversy.

title: Mehdi Mirzaei Executed in Hamedan Prison on Non-Political Charges
content:
HRANA has confirmed the identity of the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn today, Monday, October 12, as Mehdi Mirzaei.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Mr. Mirzaei had previously been arrested on charges related to non-political offenses and was subsequently sentenced to death by judicial authorities.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.

title: Japan’s Commitment to Sport Needs to Include Athlete Protection
content:
Every October, Japan celebrates Sports Day, a public holiday established to commemorate the 1964 Tokyo Olympic Games and Japan's longstanding commitment to sport as a national priority.

There has been much to celebrate in recent years. For more than six decades, Japan has had dedicated legislation – now known as the Basic Act on Sports – to advance sports on a national level. By investing in facilities, athletes’ development, and public participation—and hosting mega-events like the 2020 Olympics—Japan has become a leading sports nation.

Yet, one critical issue has received too little attention: protecting athletes and children from sports-related abuse. Human Rights Watch has documented the widespread physical, sexual, and verbal abuse many Japanese children and athletes experience when they participate in sports. A professional athlete described suffering abuses from his coach: “I was hit so many times, I can’t count ... the coach … hit [me] in the face in front of everyone. I was bleeding, but he did not stop.”

title: Lights, bells and liability: Europe’s privacy regulators crack down on smart glasses
content:
BRUSSELS — Privacy regulators want people wearing smart glasses in public to look and sound like a truck backing down a road.

Europe’s powerful data regulators have made stringent new recommendations on how smart glasses should alert people that the wearable devices are filming, including a combination of flashing lights, audio alerts and notifications sent to the phones of people nearby.

The European Data Protection Board (EDPB), made up of national privacy regulators across Europe, issued a statement about smart glasses on Tuesday, following a meeting in Brussels.

Privacy regulators are putting forward a united front on smart glasses, as privacy concerns about the wearable technology have multiplied since videos made with them have begun spreading online without the knowledge or consent of those being filmed.

The statement is not legally binding but will guide how privacy regulators in Europe assess whether smart glasses users and manufacturers are complying with EU privacy rules like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

title: Orpo: Bensapaketista uupuu perussuomalaisten kuittaus – Jani Mäkelä: Absurdia ja tavatonta
content:
Pääministeri Petteri Orpo (kok.) sanoo, että hallituksen neuvotteleman polttoainetukipaketin suuruus on 60 miljoona euroa. Hän kuvaa pakettia pieneksi.

Orpo kertoo, että kokoomus jätti ehdotuksen toimista perjantaina. Paketin ovat hyväksyneet kolme puoluetta, perussuomalaiset ei. Pääministeri odottaa puolueelta ratkaisua.

- Heille tämä on erittäin iso kysymys ja vaikea kysymys, Orpo totesi politiikan toimittajien yhdistyksen tilaisuudessa valtioneuvoston juhlahuoneistossa Smolnassa tänään alkuiltapäivästä.

Orpo ei kertonut yksityiskohtia, mistä 60 miljoonaa euroa otetaan. Hän sanoo vain, että työtä sen eteen on tehty, koska ylimääräistä liikkumavaraa ei ole.

- Aika pienestä tämä minusta on kiinni. Pitää olla vaan rohkeutta, Orpo totesi.

STT kertoi eilen, että hallituksen pöydällä olevassa paketissa on kohdennettuja toimia työmatkoihin ja ammattiliikenteeseen. Tämän pääministeri vahvisti tilaisuudessa.

title: Tesla's 'Security Protocols' Stopped DHS From Installing a Tracking Device
content:
This article was produced in collaboration with Court Watch, an independent outlet that unearths overlooked court records. Subscribe to them here.

The “security protocols” on a Tesla stopped a Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agent from placing a tracking device on it, according to a warrant reviewed by 404 Media.

On Halloween of 2025, an HSI Special Agent filed a more than 60 page application to place a tracking device on the Tesla of a suspected drug trafficker in Milwaukee. Agents had been watching alleged drug dealer Sam Stair — a local landlord they believed was using his rental properties as the front for a drug trafficking operation — for months when they asked a judge to let them install a tracker on his car. According to the warrant application, Stair went everywhere in a white Tesla and the agents wanted to see where it was when they couldn’t keep eyes on it.

title: Ukraine’s Military Recruitment: Lessons for NATO
content:
NATO’s armies are facing manpower challenges in peacetime, but Ukraine is managing to strengthen and reform its armed forces even while it is defending a 1,200 km (750-mile) frontline in an unrelenting war.

Replenishing troop numbers is one of Kyiv’s most critical challenges, especially given Russia’s numeric advantage and its sourcing of troops from abroad. The current strength of the Ukrainian Armed Forces personnel is estimated at 880,000–900,000, compared with an authorized strength of 1.55 million personnel in the Russian Armed Forces.

Ukraine is changing its approach to manning the military. A decentralized recruitment system aimed at attracting motivated volunteers has been developed since 2024. In May 2026, Kyiv announced the first phase of military reforms, which are expected to increase the number of people willing to join the armed forces.

Mobilization, which remains the cornerstone of personnel replenishment, has faced a number of challenges. Natural fatigue and the intensity of hostilities have contributed to a rise in cases of draft evasion and unauthorized absence, placing additional pressure on units already operating under extremely difficult conditions.

title: India: End Crackdown on Protesters, Arbitrary Detentions
content:
(New York) – Indian authorities are using abusive methods to crack down on thousands of peaceful protesters in New Delhi and other Indian cities, Human Rights Watch said today. The protests, led by the Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party, opposition parties, student organizations, and civil society groups, have demanded the resignation of the country’s top election official over alleged wrongdoing and the scrapping of a contentious voter list revision process.

As the protests grew in October 2026, the police have beat protesters, forcibly dragged them on the streets and stuffed them into vans and buses, arbitrarily detained them, imposed excessive restrictions on movement, and suspended mobile internet services. The authorities have also harassed and arbitrarily detained journalists covering the protests. 

“Police in Delhi are responding to peaceful protests with seemingly unnecessary or excessive force and have wrongfully detained thousands of people,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections.”

title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
content:
LONDON — Britain’s spies will have a leading role in Britain’s preparation for AI threats, the head of MI5 announced on Tuesday, after warning the technology could enable terrorists to access bioweapons.

Ken McCallum, director general of the U.K.’s domestic intelligence agency has established the AI Threat Assessment Centre to help determine how the government views potential threats.

Giving his annual threat update from MI5 headquarters in London, McCallum said: “Human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are, is capable of outthinking us.”

He stressed the “real” risks of AI, saying MI5 has caught terrorists seeking to use AI to “improve their reconnaissance and attack methodologies,” in addition to the danger of AI-enabled drones.

Though it has not yet been “realized,” he said he attaches “the greatest weight” to AI’s potential to “change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons.”

He said “low-capability” terrorists may get a “capability” uplift if the safety guardrails in AI models don’t work as intended.

title: The Anxiety Machine
content:
AI poses an existential risk to humanity. Or it will destroy all jobs. Or it will go rogue and escape control. These are headlines in reputable news outlets, but they are wrong. The mechanism that creates these concerns is a media that amplifies the fears and hostility of a class of public intellectuals and then disseminates them to an already anxious public. In some cases, AI anxiety serves the unstated financial interests of particular individuals or groups — Russia and China, for example, may try to expand these narratives — but there is usually an element of truth behind the fears, which means they cannot be immediately dismissed.

For AI, risks remain hypothetical. No one has connected the dots that show how you get from superintelligence or Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) to an existential threat. The absence of practical detail makes it likely that an existential AI threat is both hypothetical and improbable.

title: Türkiye: COP31 Host Curbs Environment Defenders
content:
(Istanbul, October 13, 2026) – The authorities in Türkiye, the host of the upcoming 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), are arbitrarily arresting and prosecuting activists and others involved in environmental protests even as the summit nears, Human Rights Watch said today.

“With Türkiye about to host the annual UN climate change summit, its environmental crackdown is a salient reminder of its intolerance of dissent,” said Deniz Bayram, assistant Europe and Central Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Turkish authorities should listen to people’s concerns about the environmental impact of activities such as mining in their areas and address them, instead of arresting and prosecuting protesters.”

In August 2026, Human Rights Watch interviewed 23 people who had been at environmental protests and reviewed relevant media reports, documents, and judicial proceedings.

title: France’s Philippe says Le Pen’s EU proposals would ‘crack open’ bloc
content:
PARIS — French center-right presidential candidate Edouard Philippe accused his far-right rival Marine Le Pen of trying to force a Frexit in disguise with her euroskeptic campaign promises.

“There is something in Marine Le Pen’s proposals that has the potential to blow Europe up, or let’s say to crack it open,” Philippe said at POLITICO’s Paris Competitiveness Summit on Tuesday.

The former prime minister — who is currently the best-placed centrist candidate to challenge the front-running Le Pen, according to recent polls — said Le Pen’s plan to unilaterally demand a drastic cut to France’s contribution to the EU budget was akin to “saying you want out of Europe” without openly advocating for leaving the bloc. Le Pen had previously called for a referendum in France on leaving the EU but dropped the proposal after her crushing defeat to Emmanuel Macron in the 2017 presidential election. Her party, the National Rally, now says it wants to change the EU from within.

title: Cops can creep on Airbnb
content:
Good Monday morning! Today's big story is an investigation from Joseph about cops and an AI tool that takes data from sites like Airbnb and Zillow and identifies specific properties. The internet is full of photos of the interiors of people's homes, from real estate and rental listings to short-term stays, and that data is in the hands of law enforcement.

And in other news, a very interesting interview with the whistleblower subject of Sorkin's new movie, some big legislative impact, and what caught my eye over the weekend around the web. Let's get into it.

An AI company now lets cops take a photo and nearly instantly figure out what specific home it was taken in, using only clues in the photo itself, and is clearly pulling data from sites like Zillow and Airbnb. 

The tool, called Raven, shows the increasing power of AI capabilities available to local law enforcement agencies. 404 Media previously reported that both the Los Angeles Police Department and Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office (MDSO) have bought access to Raven, which was previously called GeoSpy. Now, Raven, made by a company called Graylark Technologies, has added features that let cops analyze the interior of homes.

title: Pakistan: Declaration of emergency must not be pretext to crackdown on human rights
content:
Responding to the declaration of a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, as well as the imposition of governor rule and the deployment of armed forces in the province, Babu Ram Pant, Amnesty International’s Deputy Director for South Asia, said:

“Reports of arbitrary detentions of key leaders – including the provincial chief minister – and internet disruptions across the province raise concerns about the proportionality of these emergency measures. While states may, in strictly limited circumstances, derogate from their human rights obligations to respond to a public emergency that threatens the existence of the nation, emergency measures are not a blank cheque to crack down on human rights, silence dissent, or concentrate power.

“Given the history of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial executions in counterterrorism operations by the armed forces, the deployment of the army further militarizes the province and could create conditions for unlawful use of force. Pakistani authorities must avoid using military personnel for ordinary policing tasks and ensure that military forces remain accountable and comply with international human rights law and standards.
